guide.title: Riverdale, the Bronx: High Ground and Disputed Borders
guide.intro: Riverdale occupies the northwestern corner of the Bronx, bordered by Yonkers to the north, Van Cortlandt Park and Broadway to the east, the Kingsbridge neighborhood to the southeast, either the Harlem River or the Spuyten Duyvil neighborhood to the south, and the Hudson River to the west. Riverdale's boundaries are disputed, and its eastern and southern boundaries are frequently disputed. It sits at a high elevation, and its views take in the Empire State Building, the George Washington Bridge, the Hudson River and the New Jersey Palisades. Riverdale, Kingsbridge and other northwest Bronx areas were part of the Town of Yonkers until the later 19th century. ZIP codes 10463 and 10471 cover the neighborhood: 10471 lies entirely in Riverdale, while 10463 also covers the adjacent neighborhoods of Kingsbridge, Bronx, and Marble Hill, Manhattan.

sections.heading: The subsections, the river edge and the landmarked blocks
sections.body:
Riverdale is divided into subsections. Fieldston lies south of West 250th Street, east of the Henry Hudson Parkway, north of Manhattan College Parkway and west of Tibbett Avenue. Hudson Hill is above West 246th Street and west of the Henry Hudson Parkway; North Riverdale is above West 254th Street and west of Fieldston Road; Mosholu is east of Fieldston Road and above West 254th Street; Central Riverdale runs from Manhattan College Parkway to West 232nd Street; Villanova Heights is bounded by Fieldston Road, 250th Street and the Henry Hudson Parkway. Spuyten Duyvil, or South Riverdale, lies below West 232nd Street or West 239th Street, by some definitions.

Wave Hill is a 28-acre estate in the Hudson Hill section, at West 249th Street and Independence Avenue. It currently consists of public horticultural gardens and a cultural center, with two houses and a botanical garden, and on an annual basis about 65,000 people visit it. Adjacent to its grounds, Riverdale Park runs along the Hudson River for approximately 1.5 miles (2.4 km), one block wide, averaging 9 metres above sea level. The park follows Palisade Avenue between 254th Street and 232nd Street, with an entrance at Dodge Lane (247th Street), and its main sections from north to south are The North Woods, The Fishing Trail, Dodge Lane, The Oak Forest and the South End.

Christ Church Riverdale, High Victorian Gothic and built in 1866 by Richard M. Upjohn of Upjohn & Co., stands at 5040 Henry Hudson Parkway East. The Riverdale Presbyterian Church Complex, built in 1863-64 by James Renwick Jr., is at 4761-4765 Henry Hudson Parkway. The Riverdale Historic District, 15 acres in the northwest of the neighborhood, was designated on October 16, 1990. The William E. Dodge House stands at 690 W. 247th St. and the Robert Colgate House at 5225 Sycamore Ave. in Hudson Hill.

At Riverdale Avenue at W. 239th St. and Henry Hudson Pkwy., the Riverdale–Spuyten Duyvil–Kingsbridge Memorial Bell Tower — commonly the Riverdale Monument — stands in Bell Tower Park, its plaque listing World War I servicemembers from Riverdale and neighboring areas. The campus of the University of Mount Saint Vincent, at W. 261st St. and Riverdale Ave., holds Fonthill Castle; the northernmost point in New York City is at the Hudson River on that campus.

sections.heading: Yonkers, Fieldston and the estates
sections.body:
Riverdale, Kingsbridge and other northwest Bronx areas were part of the Town of Yonkers until the later 19th century.

Fieldston — the subsection south of West 250th Street, east of the Henry Hudson Parkway, north of Manhattan College Parkway and west of Tibbett Avenue — has a development history of its own. A Delafield purchase of 250 acres in 1829 gave Fieldston its name, taken from the family's Irish estate. Lots were laid out in 1909, following the extension of the IRT subway to Van Cortlandt Park–242nd Street in 1908, and Albert E. Wheeler designed Fieldston's streets to follow the land's contours. The first house was begun in 1910 and finished in 1911. In 1923, after 80 houses were completed, the Fieldston Property Owners' Association formed; it still owns Fieldston's streets and common areas, plows the streets, does sewer repair and cares for the trees. In 1938 the New York City Planning Commission approved a special zoning district there prohibiting multiple-family buildings.

The original Wave Hill House was a gray fieldstone mansion built in 1843 by William Lewis Morris. William Henry Appleton owned the estate from 1866 to 1903, enlarging the house between 1866 and 1869 and again in 1890, and George Walbridge Perkins, a partner of J. P. Morgan, purchased it in 1903. In 1960 the Perkins-Freeman family deeded Wave Hill to the City of New York. Huxley visited; the Roosevelts rented the estate in 1870 and 1871; Twain leased it from 1901 to 1903; and Toscanini lived there from 1942 to 1945.

Fonthill Castle was built in 1852 for Edwin Forrest and Catherine Norton Sinclair, a Gothic Revival cluster of six octagonal towers in hammered grey stone, its name taken from William Beckford's Fonthill Abbey. The Sisters of Charity of New York relocated the Academy of Mount Saint Vincent from McGowan's Pass to the property; that academy, founded in 1847 as a school for women, became degree-granting and took the College name in 1911, and was renamed the University of Mount Saint Vincent in 2024.

Riverdale Park was originally planned as a neighborhood centerpiece but remained undeveloped. In the 1940s the Delafield, Dodge, Douglas and Perkins families donated land to New York City with a requirement that it be kept natural, and the land was established as a special natural area in the 1950s. Wave Hill created a Learning Center connected to the park in 1981, began the Riverdale Park Project in 1983 and developed a Natural Sciences Program in 1984 — forest-management and ecological-education programs run by Wave Hill.

The Riverdale Monument was built by the architect Dwight James Baum and is dated September 17, 1930. It was moved 700 feet south from its original site in 1936 to make room for the Henry Hudson Parkway.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Van Cortlandt Park–242nd Street is the northern terminal station of the IRT Broadway–Seventh Avenue Line, served by the 1 at all times. It serves Fieldston, Kingsbridge and Riverdale, and stands on the border of Fieldston and Kingsbridge. It opened on August 1, 1908 to a design by Heins & LaFarge, is the only remaining Victorian Gothic elevated terminal station on the subway, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2005.

Metro-North's Hudson Line serves Riverdale at Riverdale station, between West 254th and 255th Streets, and at Spuyten Duyvil station, at Edsall Avenue. Riverdale station — also known as Riverdale–West 254th Street station, at Railroad Terrace and West 254th Street — is the northernmost Metro-North station in New York City on the Hudson Line. Spuyten Duyvil station is located in the Spuyten Duyvil neighborhood of the Bronx.

The Bx1, Bx7, Bx9, Bx10, Bx20, BxM1-3 and BxM18 buses serve the area, along with Bee-Line routes to Westchester County.

The 2011 Comprehensive Citywide Ferry Study identified potential ferry routes to western Manhattan and Riverdale, which were not implemented.

faq.question: How do I get to Riverdale?
faq.answer: By subway, Van Cortlandt Park–242nd Street is the northern terminal station of the IRT Broadway–Seventh Avenue Line, served by the 1 at all times, serving Fieldston, Kingsbridge and Riverdale. Metro-North's Hudson Line serves the neighborhood at Riverdale station, between West 254th and 255th Streets, and at Spuyten Duyvil station, at Edsall Avenue — though Spuyten Duyvil station is located in the Spuyten Duyvil neighborhood of the Bronx. By bus, the Bx1, Bx7, Bx9, Bx10, Bx20, BxM1-3 and BxM18 serve the area, along with Bee-Line routes to Westchester County. The 2011 Comprehensive Citywide Ferry Study identified potential ferry routes to western Manhattan and Riverdale, which were not implemented.

faq.question: Where does Riverdale begin and end?
faq.answer: Riverdale's boundaries are disputed, and its eastern and southern boundaries are frequently disputed. It is bordered by Yonkers to the north, Van Cortlandt Park and Broadway to the east, the Kingsbridge neighborhood to the southeast, either the Harlem River or the Spuyten Duyvil neighborhood to the south, and the Hudson River to the west. Its subsections are Fieldston, Hudson Hill, North Riverdale, Mosholu, Central Riverdale, Spuyten Duyvil or South Riverdale, and Villanova Heights.

faq.question: What is Wave Hill?
faq.answer: A 28-acre estate in the Hudson Hill section of Riverdale, at West 249th Street and Independence Avenue, which currently consists of public horticultural gardens and a cultural center with two houses and a botanical garden. About 65,000 people visit on an annual basis. The original Wave Hill House was a gray fieldstone mansion built in 1843 by William Lewis Morris; George Walbridge Perkins, a partner of J. P. Morgan, bought the estate in 1903, and the Perkins-Freeman family deeded it to the City of New York in 1960. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1983, and Wave Hill House was designated a New York City Landmark on June 21, 1966.

faq.question: What is Fonthill Castle?
faq.answer: A Gothic Revival building on the campus of the University of Mount Saint Vincent at W. 261st St. and Riverdale Ave., built in 1852 for Edwin Forrest and Catherine Norton Sinclair as a cluster of six octagonal towers in hammered grey stone, named after William Beckford's Fonthill Abbey. Its design has been attributed to Alexander Jackson Davis and also to Thomas C. Smith. The castle has served as a convent, chapel, museum, chaplain's residence and the college library, and later housed the admissions office. It held the library from 1942 to 1968 and is currently vacant.

faq.question: Which Riverdale buildings and districts are landmarked?
faq.answer: The Riverdale Historic District, 15 acres in the northwest of the neighborhood, was designated on October 16, 1990. Wave Hill House was designated a New York City Landmark on June 21, 1966 and Wave Hill was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1983. Fonthill Castle was designated on March 15, 1966 and National Register-listed on July 11, 1980. Riverdale Presbyterian Church was designated on April 19, 1966 and listed on October 14, 1982; Christ Church on January 11, 1967 and listed on September 8, 1983. The William E. Dodge House was listed on August 28, 1977, the Robert Colgate House on September 8, 1983, and the Riverdale Monument on January 3, 2012.

photos.title: Wave Hill House
photos.description: The entrance front of Wave Hill House, a gray fieldstone building of two main storeys under a slate hipped roof with dormers, tall stone chimneys and a low roofline balustrade. White-shuttered sash windows flank a columned entrance porch, and clipped shrubs and planting beds line the drive in front of the house under an overcast sky.
photos.author: Andre Carrotflower

places.name: University of Mount Saint Vincent
places.address: W. 261st St. and Riverdale Ave., Bronx, NY
places.summary: A university situated in Riverdale, Bronx, affiliated with the Sisters of Charity of New York, whose campus holds Fonthill Castle. The northernmost point in New York City is at the Hudson River on the campus. Fonthill Castle was designated a New York City Landmark on March 15, 1966 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 11, 1980, reference number 80002585.
places.history:
The institution was founded in 1847 as the Academy of Mount Saint Vincent, a school for women. It became a degree-granting institution and took the College name in 1911, was known as the College of Mount Saint Vincent from 1911 to 2023, and was renamed the University of Mount Saint Vincent in 2024.

Fonthill Castle was built in 1852 for Edwin Forrest and Catherine Norton Sinclair. It is a Gothic Revival building consisting of a cluster of six octagonal towers, built of hammered grey stone, and its name derives from William Beckford's Gothic Fonthill Abbey in England. Its design has been attributed to Alexander Jackson Davis and also to Thomas C. Smith.

The Sisters of Charity of New York relocated the Academy of Mount Saint Vincent from McGowan's Pass to the property. The castle has served as a convent, chapel, museum, chaplain's residence and the college library, and later came to house the admissions office. It housed the library from 1942 to 1968 and is currently vacant.

places.name: Christ Church Riverdale
places.address: 5040 Henry Hudson Parkway East, Bronx, NY
places.summary: A historic Episcopal parish church at 5040 Henry Hudson Parkway East in Riverdale, Bronx. It is High Victorian Gothic, built in 1866 by the architect Richard M. Upjohn of Upjohn & Co.
places.history: The church was designated a New York City Landmark on January 11, 1967 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 8, 1983, reference number 83001637.

photos.title: Christ Church Riverdale
photos.description: Christ Church seen from across the street. The stone gable end carries a pointed-arch window with stone tracery and a bellcote above holding a visible bell and topped by a cross. Bands of contrasting stone run through the masonry, a lower stone building with a pointed-arch porch adjoins at the left, and an iron fence, shrubs and parked cars line the sidewalk in front.
photos.author: Andre Carrotflower

places.name: Riverdale Presbyterian Church
places.summary: A historic Presbyterian church in the Riverdale neighborhood of the Bronx, carried on the National Register as the Riverdale Presbyterian Church Complex at 4761-4765 Henry Hudson Parkway. It was built in 1863-64, in Late Gothic Revival and Stick style, by the architect James Renwick Jr., with a later enlargement in 1936 credited to Dwight James Baum.
places.history: The church was designated a New York City Landmark on April 19, 1966 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places on October 14, 1982, reference number 82001092.

places.summary: A house at 690 W. 247th St. in Riverdale, listed on the National Register of Historic Places on August 28, 1977, reference number 77000934.

places.name: Robert Colgate House
places.summary: A house at 5225 Sycamore Ave. in the Hudson Hill section of Riverdale, listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 8, 1983, reference number 83001638.

places.name: Riverdale Monument
places.address: Riverdale Avenue at W. 239th St. & Henry Hudson Pkwy., Bronx, NY
places.summary: The Riverdale–Spuyten Duyvil–Kingsbridge Memorial Bell Tower, commonly known as the Riverdale Monument, in Bell Tower Park, located in the Riverdale section of the Bronx. Its plaque lists World War I servicemembers from Riverdale and neighboring areas.
places.history: The monument was built by the architect Dwight James Baum and is dated September 17, 1930. It was moved 700 feet south from its original site in 1936 to make room for the Henry Hudson Parkway, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on January 3, 2012.

photos.title: Riverdale Monument bell tower
photos.description: The memorial bell tower, a tall square shaft of rough stone masonry rising from a low stone wall. Paired pointed-arch belfry openings sit near the top beneath a crenellated cap, narrow slit windows pierce the shaft, and three pointed-arch recessed panels are set into the base. Bare winter trees stand behind it and green highway signs are visible at the right against a clear blue sky.
photos.author: Jim.henderson
